title: Admin Task Compiler: convert ad-hoc runbooks to executable task graphs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Runbooks exist as a mix of markdown documents, ad-hoc scripts, and on-call tribal knowledge. Engineers and SREs spend time translating these artifacts into manual step sequences during incidents which increases MTTR and causes inconsistent outcomes. Goal: Build an "admin task compiler" that ingests common runbook formats (markdown + code snippets, legacy admin scripts, and curated operator notes) and emits an executable directed acyclic graph (DAG) of discrete tasks with explicit inputs/outputs, retries, and safety gates. 

Scope: 1) Parser for internal runbook markdown conventions and tagged script blocks. 2) Intermediate task-graph model with step metadata (timeout, retry, required approvals). 3) Execution harness that runs steps as idempotent tasks (shell, kubectl, API calls) with a sandboxed runner and audit logs. 4) A dry-run simulator UI to visualize graphs before executing in-prod. 5) Safety features: transactional checkpoints, automatic rollback hooks, and mandatory approval nodes for risky steps.

Out-of-scope for MVP: full natural-language to task translation, integration with third-party incident tools (will be separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Compiler can parse 3 canonical runbook styles used by Redwood and emit a task-graph JSON schema
Execution harness runs a task graph in 'dry-run' mode and produces a step-by-step simulated log without side effects
Production runner executes simple graphs against a staging cluster with audit logs persisted to internal S3 and shows status in the console
Safety gates enforce approval nodes and prevent execution when approval is missing; rollback hooks can be attached to steps
End-to-end demo completed with support team and runbook converted from 'Incident: DB failover' doc
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use a lightweight, JSON-first intermediate format rather than a heavyweight DSL to maximize interoperability with Console and Ops Playbooks
Decision: Start with existing markdown conventions (---meta--- code fences with tags) to accelerate parsing; follow-up work will add an authoring UI
Trade-off: MVP will execute containerized steps via our existing task-runner binary rather than reimplementing per-step connectors
Security note: execution runner will run in a dedicated service account with least-privilege IAM and KMS-wrapped credentials for any secrets
implementation_steps: Inventory common runbook docs and pick 3 canonical examples (DB failover, cache flush, model reload)
Design intermediate graph schema and map markdown patterns to graph constructs
Prototype parser + serializer and add unit tests for edge cases (conditional branches, input prompts)
Integrate with task-runner for sandboxed dry-runs; add telemetry hooks for step timings and outcomes
Build simple Console visualization for graph preview and approval workflow
Conduct tabletop with SRE and support to validate safety flows; iterate on approvals and rollback UX
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect parsing could lead to missing safety steps. Mitigation: require a human approval node for any conversion where automated confidence < 0.95 and provide side-by-side diff for reviewer
Risk: Runner could accidentally run destructive commands. Mitigation: enforce dry-run by default and sandbox system calls; destructive commands must be whitelisted per project
Risk: Secrets exposure during execution. Mitigation: never inline secrets in compiled graphs; reference secrets by name and resolve at runtime via KMS and ephemeral tokens
